library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Cojutti_2026_fosfomycin"))
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-025-01586-1>
* Description: `r mod$description`

Cojutti 2026 fitted plasma and prostate-tissue fosfomycin concentrations
jointly in Monolix 2023R1. Plasma is a one-compartment model with first-order
absorption. Prostate tissue is linked to plasma by a *direct-response power
function*, so the prostate concentration is an algebraic function of the
plasma concentration and has no ODE state of its own:

$$C_{prostate}(t) = PR \cdot C_c(t)^{POW}$$

Twelve candidate structures were compared (one or two compartments; a
proportional, power or saturable link; `ka` estimated or fixed). The selected
structure is model 5 of the paper's Table S1 (electronic supplementary
material, ESM): one compartment, a power link, and `ka` fixed. The ESM
supplies the final Monolix code, whose `EQUATION:` block is the source for
both equations in the model file:

```
Cc = pkmodel(ka, V, Cl)
Cp = PR*(Cc^POW)
```

# Population

104 men undergoing endoscopic surgery for benign prostatic hyperplasia at a
single Italian centre (Bologna, February 2022 to September 2023). 85 (81.7%)
had Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate and 19 (18.3%) had transurethral
resection. Median (range): age 70 (49-84) years, weight 78 (60-107) kg, BMI
26.3 (20.6-41.5) kg/m^2, CKD-EPI eGFR 78.5 (34-102) mL/min/1.73 m^2, prostate
volume 75 (20-220) mL, PSA 3.10 (0.02-66) ng/mL (Results, first paragraph).

Every patient took oral fosfomycin trometamol 3 g 12 h before the end of the
prophylactic scheme and 3 g at its end (`t = -12 h` and `t = 0 h`). Each
contributed exactly one plasma sample and one concomitant prostate biopsy, at
a median of 3.86 (0.42-10.7) h after the second dose. There were no samples
during absorption, which is why `ka` and its variability had to be fixed.

```{r population}
str(mod$population)
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lka` (ka, 1/h) | 0.92, fixed | Table 1; Methods 2.2 (value from healthy volunteers, ref. 23) |
| `lcl` (CL/F, L/h) | 14.68 (RSE 14.4%) | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (V/F at 0 kg, L) | 60.86 (RSE 44.1%) | Table 1; Results equation `V = 60.86 x e^(0.02 x BW)` |
| `e_wt_vc` (1/kg) | 0.02 (RSE 26.9%) | Table 1, `beta_V_weight` |
| `lrprostate` (PR) | 0.26 (RSE 7.09%) | Table 1; footnote "penetration ratio at a plasma concentration of 1 mg/L" |
| `lpow_prostate` (POW) | 1.57 (RSE 1.80%) | Table 1 |
| `etalka` | SD 1.09, fixed | Table 1, `omega_ka` |
| `etalcl` | SD 0.76 (CV 87.86%) | Table 1, `omega_CL`; CV from ESM Table S3 |
| `etalvc` | SD 0.38 (CV 39.52%) | Table 1, `omega_V`; ESM Table S3 |
| `etalrprostate` | SD 0.42 (CV 44.27%) | Table 1, `omega_PR`; ESM Table S3 |
| `etalpow_prostate` | SD 0.095 (CV 9.5%) | Table 1, `omega_POW`; ESM Table S3 |
| `addSd` (mg/L) | 1.35 (RSE 20.5%) | Table 1, `a_plasma` (constant error) |
| `addSd_Cprostate` (ug/g) | 1.01 (RSE 34.0%) | Table 1, `a_prostate` (constant error) |
| One-compartment first-order absorption | -- | ESM model code, `Cc = pkmodel(ka, V, Cl)` |
| Weight on V/F | `V = 60.86 * exp(0.02 * WT)` | Results, "Model equations" |
| Prostate link | `Cprostate = PR * Cc^POW` | Methods 2.2 model (2); Results `Cp = 0.26 x Cc^1.57`; ESM model code |

Table 1 lists the random effects as **standard deviations** on the log scale.
The ESM Table S3 prints a CV column next to each one, and that column matches
`sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)` to the rounding of the printed SDs, which confirms
they are SDs rather than variances. The model file therefore squares each
value.

```{r omega-check}
omega <- c(ka = 1.09, V = 0.38, CL = 0.76, PR = 0.42, POW = 0.095)
# Half a unit in the last printed decimal of each SD.
half_ulp <- c(ka = 0.005, V = 0.005, CL = 0.005, PR = 0.005, POW = 0.0005)
cv_published <- c(ka = 151.02, V = 39.52, CL = 87.86, PR = 44.27, POW = 9.5)
# The CV column was computed from the unrounded SDs, so invert it and check
# that the result rounds to the printed SD. Read as variances instead, the
# same CVs would need omega = 1.19, 0.15, 0.57, 0.18 and 0.009.
sd_from_cv <- sqrt(log(1 + (cv_published / 100)^2))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(omega_SD = omega, CV_published = cv_published, SD_from_CV = sd_from_cv) |>
    dplyr::rename("omega, Table 1 (SD)" = omega_SD, "CV, ESM Table S3 (%)" = CV_published, "sqrt(log(1 + CV^2))" = SD_from_CV),
  digits = 4
)
stopifnot(all(abs(sd_from_cv - omega) <= half_ulp + 1e-9))
```

# The printed equations reproduce the paper's own medians

The volume equation uses **absolute** body weight with no centring, so the
typical value of 60.86 L applies to a 0 kg patient. Evaluated at the cohort's
median weight of 78 kg, it gives the paper's separately reported median
individual apparent volume of 288.9 L. That agreement confirms the exponential
form on uncentred weight. The Methods text calls the covariate model "a power
function", but a power model, or a model centred on the median, would put the
typical V/F at 60.86 L.

The link function evaluated at the observed median plasma concentration
(11.1 mg/L) gives a prostate concentration close to the observed median
(11.6 ug/g). The implied ratio of 1.03 is close to the reported median
observed prostate-to-plasma ratio of 1.04.

```{r equation-check}
v_at_median_wt <- 60.86 * exp(0.02 * 78)
cp_at_median_cc <- 0.26 * 11.1^1.57
knitr::kable(tibble::tribble(
  ~Quantity, ~Published, ~Model,
  "Median individual V/F at 78 kg (L)", 288.9, v_at_median_wt,
  "Prostate conc. at plasma 11.1 mg/L (ug/g)", 11.6, cp_at_median_cc,
  "Prostate/plasma ratio at plasma 11.1 mg/L", 1.04, cp_at_median_cc / 11.1
), digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  abs(v_at_median_wt / 288.9 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(cp_at_median_cc / 11.6 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

# Mass balance under typical values

CL and V are apparent oral parameters (F = 1), so after a single 3 g dose the
typical-value plasma AUC(0-inf) must equal Dose / CL = 3000 / 14.68 =
204.4 mg h/L, whatever the body weight. Both sides use the same typical
parameters, so the difference is pure numerical error and a tight bound is
appropriate. The check also confirms that the two ODE states are the two
named compartments in order.

```{r typical}
# The model declares two residual-error endpoints (Cc and Cprostate), so every
# observation row must nominate one: observation rows sit on the central
# state with dvid = 1. Both Cc and Cprostate are returned as columns at every
# observation time whichever endpoint is nominated.
# useLinCmt = FALSE keeps the explicit ODEs rather than an analytic solution.
t_single <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2, 24, by = 0.1), seq(24, 300, by = 1))))
ev_single <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 3000, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = t_single, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_single,
  params = c(WT = 78), useLinCmt = FALSE
) |> as.data.frame()

stopifnot(identical(mod$state, c("depot", "central")))
# The prostate output is exactly the power link of the plasma output.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(typ$Cprostate, 0.26 * typ$Cc^1.57, tolerance = 1e-8)))

nca_typ <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(typ |> dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc), Cc ~ time | id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 3000), amt ~ time | id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
) |>
  PKNCA::pk.nca() |>
  as.data.frame()
auc_typ <- nca_typ$PPORRES[nca_typ$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"]
c(AUCinf = auc_typ, Dose_over_CL = 3000 / 14.68)
stopifnot(abs(auc_typ / (3000 / 14.68) - 1) < 0.005)
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper reports body weight only as a median and range (78, 60-107 kg).
Weight is drawn from a log-normal centred on 78 kg, and draws outside the
observed range are rejected and redrawn rather than clamped to it, so that the
cohort's median is not distorted. The same weights are reused for all three
dosing schemes of the paper's Monte Carlo simulation (Methods 2.4):

* **A**: 3 g at `t = -12 h` and 3 g at `t = 0 h` (the studied scheme);
* **B**: 3 g at `t = -12 h` and 6 g at `t = 0 h`;
* **C**: 3 g at `t = -8 h` and 6 g at `t = 0 h`.

In the event tables the first dose is at time 0, so `t = 0 h` of the paper is
time 12 here.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_per_arm <- 200L

draw_wt <- function(n, median_wt = 78, sdlog = 0.14, lower = 60, upper = 107) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- stats::rlnorm(2L * n, log(median_wt), sdlog)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lower & x <= upper])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}
wt <- draw_wt(n_per_arm)

schemes <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scheme, ~t_first, ~amt_first, ~amt_second,
  "A: 3 g t-12h + 3 g t0h", 0, 3000, 3000,
  "B: 3 g t-12h + 6 g t0h", 0, 3000, 6000,
  "C: 3 g t-8h + 6 g t0h", 4, 3000, 6000
)

obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), seq(12, 24, by = 0.05))))

make_arm <- function(k) {
  s <- schemes[k, ]
  ids <- (k - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, dose_no = 1:2) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = ifelse(dose_no == 1, s$t_first, 12),
      amt = ifelse(dose_no == 1, s$amt_first, s$amt_second),
      evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-dose_no)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_grid) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scheme = s$scheme, WT = wt[id - (k - 1L) * n_per_arm]) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(schemes)), make_arm))
stopifnot(
  anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]) == 0L,
  dplyr::n_distinct(events$id) == 3L * n_per_arm
)
summary(wt)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = c("scheme", "WT"), useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad2 = time - 12)
```

The paper reports the median of the individual (post hoc) apparent V and CL
as 288.9 L and 15.7 L/h. The simulated cohort's medians should be close.
They are not identical: the post hoc estimates are shrunk towards the typical
values, and the simulated weights only reproduce the cohort's median and range.
With a CL/F variability of SD 0.76 the median of 200 subjects carries a
standard error of about 7%, so the bound is 25%; a mis-transcribed CL or V
moves the median by far more.

```{r median-params}
indiv <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^A", scheme)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, vc, cl)
med_check <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter, ~Published, ~Simulated,
  "Median individual V/F (L)", 288.9, stats::median(indiv$vc),
  "Median individual CL/F (L/h)", 15.7, stats::median(indiv$cl)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (Simulated / Published - 1))
knitr::kable(med_check, digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(med_check$`Difference (%)`) < 25))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2: plasma and prostate profiles for the studied scheme

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Cojutti 2026: simulated fosfomycin plasma (mg/L) and prostate (ug/g) concentrations after 3 g at t = -12 h and 3 g at t = 0 h. Lines are medians; ribbons are 5th-95th percentiles."}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^A", scheme)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cprostate), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(matrix = dplyr::recode(matrix, Cc = "Plasma (mg/L)", Cprostate = "Prostate (ug/g)")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(matrix, tad2) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = stats::quantile(conc, 0.05), q50 = stats::median(conc), q95 = stats::quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad2, q50, colour = matrix, fill = matrix)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("firebrick", "goldenrod")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("firebrick", "goldenrod")) +
  labs(x = "Time relative to the second dose (h)", y = "Fosfomycin concentration", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Figure 3: prostate-to-plasma penetration ratio

Figure 3 is a histogram of the simulated penetration ratio
(`Cprostate / Cc`) for the studied scheme. The text reports the share of
simulated subjects in three bins. The time at which the ratio is evaluated is
not stated, so it is taken here at the study's median sampling time (the
3.85 h grid point, nearest to the 3.86 h median after the second dose). Under the power link the ratio is
`PR * Cc^(POW - 1)`, so it rises with the plasma concentration. A wrong `POW`
or `PR` therefore moves all three bins together. With 200 subjects the
binomial standard error of each share is about 3.5 percentage points, so the
tolerance is 12 percentage points.

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Cojutti 2026: distribution of the simulated prostate-to-plasma penetration ratio, 3.86 h after the second 3 g dose."}
ratio_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^A", scheme), abs(tad2 - 3.85) < 1e-6) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = Cprostate / Cc)
stopifnot(nrow(ratio_df) == n_per_arm)

ratio_bins <- tibble::tibble(
  Bin = c("< 1", "1 - 2", "> 2"),
  Published = c(48.3, 37.5, 14.2),
  Simulated = 100 * c(
    mean(ratio_df$ratio < 1),
    mean(ratio_df$ratio >= 1 & ratio_df$ratio <= 2),
    mean(ratio_df$ratio > 2)
  )
)
knitr::kable(ratio_bins |> dplyr::rename("Penetration ratio" = Bin, "Published (%)" = Published, "Simulated (%)" = Simulated), digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(ratio_bins$Simulated - ratio_bins$Published) < 12))

ggplot(ratio_df, aes(ratio)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, boundary = 0, fill = "grey60", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(1, 2), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Prostate-to-plasma penetration ratio", y = "Simulated subjects") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA table. PKNCA is used here to compute each subject's
plasma and prostate exposure over the 12 h vulnerable period after the second
dose (time 12-24 in the event tables), grouped by dosing scheme. The plasma
AUC over that window drives the probability of target attainment (PTA) below.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- function(df, conc_col) {
  out <- df |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, scheme, conc = dplyr::all_of(conc_col))
  # Guarantee a pre-dose time-zero row per subject (extravascular, so 0).
  dplyr::bind_rows(out, out |> dplyr::distinct(id, scheme) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)) |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, scheme, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::arrange(scheme, id, time)
}
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, scheme)
intervals_vp <- data.frame(start = 12, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

run_nca <- function(conc_col) {
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input(sim, conc_col), conc ~ time | scheme + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | scheme + id),
    intervals = intervals_vp
  ) |>
    PKNCA::pk.nca() |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(matrix = conc_col)
}
nca_res <- dplyr::bind_rows(run_nca("Cc"), run_nca("Cprostate"))

nca_res |>
  dplyr::group_by(matrix, scheme, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = stats::median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Matrix" = matrix, "Scheme" = scheme,
    "AUC 0-12 h after dose 2" = auclast, "Cmax" = cmax, "Tmax after dose 2 (h)" = tmax
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

## Figure 4A: PTA of AUC/MIC > 83.3

Methods 2.4 defines the AUC target on the *plasma* concentration-time curve,
over the 12 h vulnerable period after the second dose. The paper states that
the PTA was optimal (at least 90%) up to an MIC of 0.5 mg/L for scheme A, and
up to 1 mg/L for schemes B and C. A PTA of at least 90% at a given MIC is the
same as the 10th percentile of AUC exceeding 83.3 x MIC. Each statement
therefore brackets that percentile within a factor of two. The paper
simulated 1000 subjects per scheme and this vignette 200, and the 10th
percentile of 200 subjects carries a sampling error of about 10%, so each
bound is relaxed by 25%:

* **A**: `83.3 x 0.5 < P10(AUC) < 83.3 x 1`;
* **B and C**: `83.3 x 1 < P10(AUC) < 83.3 x 2`.

A robust quantile is checked rather than the PTA percentage, because a
threshold-crossing percentage changes abruptly near the threshold.

```{r fig4a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4A of Cojutti 2026: probability of attaining a plasma AUC(0-12 h after the second dose)/MIC above 83.3, by dosing scheme. The dotted line marks the 90% optimality threshold."}
auc_vp <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(matrix == "Cc", PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(id, scheme, auc = PPORRES)

pta_bracket <- auc_vp |>
  dplyr::group_by(scheme) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p10_auc = stats::quantile(auc, 0.1), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    optimal_mic_published = ifelse(grepl("^A", scheme), 0.5, 1),
    lower = 83.3 * optimal_mic_published,
    upper = 83.3 * 2 * optimal_mic_published
  )
knitr::kable(
  pta_bracket |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Scheme" = scheme, "P10 plasma AUC (mg h/L)" = p10_auc,
      "Highest optimal MIC, published (mg/L)" = optimal_mic_published,
      "Required P10 lower bound" = lower, "Required P10 upper bound" = upper
    ),
  digits = 1
)
stopifnot(all(pta_bracket$p10_auc > pta_bracket$lower / 1.25 & pta_bracket$p10_auc < pta_bracket$upper * 1.25))

mics <- 2^seq(-4, 4)
tidyr::expand_grid(auc_vp, mic = mics) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scheme, mic) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta = 100 * mean(auc / mic > 83.3), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(mic, pta, colour = scheme)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = mics, labels = format(mics, drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Figure 4B-D: 70% time above MIC in the prostate

For scheme A the paper reports optimal PTAs of 70% time above the MIC in
prostate tissue for the whole 12 h vulnerable period against MICs up to
1 mg/L, and for only part of it (2-5 h) against MICs up to 4 mg/L. The
simulation is consistent with both statements: the PTA over the whole window
is at least 90% at 1 mg/L and below 90% at 4 mg/L, and both are asserted.
The figure resolves the PTA over time; the 2-5 h sub-window is not checked.

```{r fig4b}
ft_pta <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(tad2 >= 0, tad2 <= 12) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(mic = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scheme, id, mic) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ft = mean(Cprostate > mic), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::group_by(scheme, mic) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta = 100 * mean(ft >= 0.7), .groups = "drop")
pta_a <- ft_pta |> dplyr::filter(grepl("^A", scheme))
stopifnot(
  pta_a$pta[pta_a$mic == 1] >= 90,
  pta_a$pta[pta_a$mic == 4] < 90
)
ft_pta |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = mic, values_from = pta, names_prefix = "MIC ") |>
  dplyr::rename("Scheme" = scheme) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "PTA (%) of 70% time above MIC in prostate tissue over the 12 h after the second dose.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **New parameter names.** `PR` and `POW` are carried as `lrprostate` and
  `lpow_prostate`. These are the prostate members of the `relf` / `pow_elf`
  family used for the same power-function direct-response link to epithelial
  lining fluid (Dimelow 2018 avibactam).
- **The Monolix model header is library boilerplate.** The `DESCRIPTION:`
  block of the ESM model code says "administration is via a bolus" and "the
  PD model is a direct Emax model". Both statements are contradicted by the
  `EQUATION:` block directly beneath them, which uses `pkmodel(ka, V, Cl)` and
  a power link with no Emax or EC50. The equations were followed.
- **Covariate form.** The Methods text describes the covariate model as "a
  power function". The printed final equation is exponential on uncentred
  body weight, and only the exponential form reproduces the reported median
  individual V/F (see above). The equation was followed.
- **Table 1 bootstrap column.** The bootstrap median of `beta_V_weight` is
  printed as 0.17, outside its own bootstrap range of 0.004-0.03 (probably
  0.017). The model uses the population estimate 0.02, so this does not
  affect it.
- **Prostate units.** Prostate concentrations are in ug/g of tissue and
  plasma concentrations in mg/L. `PR` therefore carries mixed units, and the
  "penetration ratio" is a ratio of ug/g to mg/L, as in the paper.
- **Virtual weights.** The paper reports body weight only as a median and
  range. The log-normal spread (`sdlog = 0.14`) is the maintainers' choice.
- **Figure 3 time point.** The paper does not state when the simulated
  penetration ratio is evaluated. The median sampling time (3.86 h after the
  second dose) is assumed.
- **AUC target matrix.** Methods 2.4 defines the AUC/MIC target on the plasma
  curve, while the Figure 4 caption places both targets "in the prostate".
  The plasma reading is used for the AUC target because it is the one the
  Methods define. The 70% time-above-MIC target is evaluated in prostate
  tissue.
- **Table 2 not reproduced.** The cumulative fractions of response weight
  the PTA by the EUCAST MIC frequency distributions of *E. coli*. Those
  distributions are not printed in the paper.
- **Cohort size.** The paper simulated 1000 subjects per scheme; this
  vignette uses 200 per scheme.
